summary: Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and with traditional teachers including Geshe Wangyal. He co-founded the translation bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Alexander Coburn Soper worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Hamilton College and Princeton University. He taught at Bryn Mawr College, was appointed professor at New York University in 1960, and edited Artibus Asiae (1958–1993).

Alexander Cunningham specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Christ's Hospital, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and under James Prinsep. He founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its first director (1861–1865) and later Director-General (1871–1885).
Alexander Duff was a scholar in religious studies and history and archaeology. He was educated at the University of Aberdeen and the University of St Andrews from circa 1821 to 1829.
Alexander Freiman studied under Christian Bartholomae from circa 1906 to 1907 and under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy.

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr., also studying under Robert H. Sharf and Janet Gyatso, and joined the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander Hamilton was an Indologist. He served at the East India Company College, becoming Professor of Sanskrit in 1806 and Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature in 1808.
Alexander James O'Neill works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued PhD candidacy at the University of Toronto and held a post as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Christian Friedrich Schwarz, at the University of Göttingen, and at Lincoln's Inn. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819) and founded the Royal Asiatic Society.

Alexander Kabanoff worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He held posts at Kazan Imperial University from circa 1826 to 1849 and at Imperial St. Petersburg University from circa 1849 to 1870.

Alexander Lubotsky specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, becoming full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison, attested in 2013.
Alexander Murray was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1794 to 1801 and later held a post there from circa 1812 to 1813.

Alexander O. Hsu specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer (~2011–2018), and held a teaching post at North Dakota State University (~2019–2020).

Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Moscow State University, worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968), and was Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia at SOAS University of London (1990–2001).
Alexander Rogers worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at East India Company College from circa 1843 to 1845 and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1845 to 1878.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied for a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh under supervisors Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw, attested in 2008.
Alexander Studholme is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin.

Alexander W. Macdonald was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the CNRS (~1956–1989), the Musée de l'Homme, and served as Professor at Paris Nanterre University (~1975–1991).
